svg.title: How test 2 mechanically checks for the five literal edge strings
svg.desc: Top half shows the CAUSAL_EDGES dictionary as it appears in NB04 source code with five highlighted dictionary entries each mapping a string node name to a list containing one downstream node name; bottom half shows five literal substring search operations one per edge each finding its target literal exactly in the source string and reporting found with a green checkmark.
svg.text: Test 2 mechanics — five literal `in source` checks
NB04 source (after _read_notebook_source returns one big string):
Five literal substrings, each must be found inside that source:
No regex. Just `assert edge in source` — plain Python substring containment, the simplest check there is.
If even one literal is missing, the loop's `assert` fails on that iteration and the test reports which edge.
The five literals include their quotes, colon, spaces, and brackets — exact dict formatting matters.
